title: WhatsappBridgeChannelConfig
description: TOML config for one wcore-channel-whatsapp instance driven through the Wayland Desktop WhatsApp bridge (Node subprocess, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio). OPT-IN: a channel with no `backend` key, or `backend = "meta-business"`, uses the native Cloud API adapter and needs no Node. Carries no secrets — the bridged backends authenticate by QR pairing and persist their own session material under session_dir.

backend.description: Which bridged backend to drive. Both are UNOFFICIAL WhatsApp Web clients: Meta does not support them and bans accounts for automated use — see docs/whatsapp-bridge.md. `meta-business` is deliberately absent from this enum: it is served by the native Cloud API adapter (WhatsappChannelConfig), not through the bridge.

bridge_path.description: Absolute path to the operator's bridge.js. wayland-core does not ship, download or install the bridge; this path must name an existing file whose Node dependencies are already installed.

node_path.description: Explicit Node interpreter to run the bridge with. When unset, `node` is resolved from PATH (PATHEXT is honoured on Windows). When neither resolves, the channel fails closed naming node_runtime and never reports healthy.

session_dir.description: Directory the bridge persists pairing and session material under, passed as --session. When unset, the bridge chooses its own default beneath the user's home directory.

workspace_name.description: Human-readable label. Used for logging only.

default_recipient.description: Fallback WhatsApp chat id used when an OutgoingMessage arrives with an empty conversation_id. For the bridged backends this is a JID (e.g. 15555550100@s.whatsapp.net), not an E.164 number.

handshake_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the `health` handshake that confirms which backend the bridge actually loaded. Node cold start on a loaded host is not fast.

rpc_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for any other RPC reply before giving up on it.

max_message_chars.description: Width to chunk a single message at, in characters. When unset the channel uses BRIDGE_UNMEASURED_CHUNK_WIDTH (4096), which is a CHUNKING POLICY and not a measured or documented WhatsApp limit: neither baileys nor whatsapp-web.js nor WhatsApp publishes a body limit for the Web/multi-device protocol these backends speak, and the 4096 this replaced was borrowed from Meta's Cloud API page, which governs a different surface. Set this only from a boundary you have actually driven against your own paired bridge — too high is the direction that loses messages. Zero is refused, and it is refused by the deserializer in bridge/mod.rs, NOT by this file: config_schema() hands this schema to a host for display and nothing in the product validates a config against it. The minimum below documents the bound; it does not impose it.
